answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce token for a fixed period before it can place trades, with larger credit limits earned only through transactions that counterparties later confirm. A fake agent may create many accounts, but each one ties up real capital and must build a separate record; recycling funds is limited while locks overlap. The prism of incentives is that honest activity releases collateral over time, while a coordinated tide of disposable identities risks forfeiture and lost liquidity. Quartz-hard rules make identities costly, not impossible.
